observed channels cover all mechanisms the IXIT would list
use case of each observed channel inferred from endpoints and protocol

summary: Check functionally, e.g. by sniffing handshakes or trying downgrades, that the device actually uses the documented cryptographic settings.

units.note: Compare used crypto with IXIT; sniffing suffices, downgrade attempts are active.

outside_procedure_cues: Negotiated TLS versions, cipher suites, certificate key types and plaintext flows are visible at the gateway but cannot be set against the IXIT.
rationale: Only verdict bullet compares observed settings with IXIT documentation; under R1 nothing is reachable.

summary: Check that every documented network and security implementation was reviewed or evaluated and that the review covers its scope.

units.note: Implementation list and review method come from the supplier.
Report scope compared with the implementation description.

outside_procedure_cues: Handshake fingerprints, protocol banners or User-Agent strings may hint at the library in use, which could be looked up in public certification lists.
rationale: Showing that an implementation lacks any review needs supplier reports; public sources cannot prove absence of review, and coverage of all implementations is unknowable passively.

summary: Check that name and version of each reviewed implementation on the device match those in its review report.

units.note: Read implementation identity from the device and compare with supplied report.

outside_procedure_cues: Version strings in banners, User-Agent headers or update requests may reveal implementation identity, but the supplier report to compare against is unavailable.
rationale: First bullet compares with supplier-provided reports (R1). The alternative PASS bullet needs proof the device exposes no identification, which passive absence cannot establish.

summary: Check that every component using cryptography has a referenced update mechanism and that replacement side effects were considered.

units.note: Software component list and update references from supplier.
Manufacturer consideration of side effects of replacing algorithms.

outside_procedure_cues: Observed firmware update downloads show an update channel exists; a change of offered suites after an update would hint at replaceable cryptography.
rationale: Both criteria concern supplier documentation and manufacturer reasoning; no network-observable property decides them.
